# cattery

cattery: NixOS, nix-darwin, and home-manager modules organized as room profiles

# cattery

cattery is a collection of 262 Nix modules for NixOS, nix-darwin, and home-manager. The modules are grouped into rooms: named sets of modules that enable each other with shared defaults. Enable a room to turn on a group of related features, then override the individual modules you want to change.

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs.cattery-modules.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/cattery-modules/*.tar.gz";

  outputs = { nixpkgs, cattery-modules, ... }: {
    nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      modules = [ cattery-modules.nixosModules.default ];
    };
  };
}
```

```nix
# configuration.nix
{ config, ... }: {
  cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
}
```

`cattery.room.desktop.dev` enables the desktop chain and a set of developer tools. See [Rooms](/rooms) for the full contents of each room.

***

## What is a room?

A room is a module that enables other modules with `lib.mkDefault`. It does not add configuration of its own. Enabling a room also enables the rooms it depends on. This is the NixOS graph:

```
room.basis
 ├─ room.general                 (basis + boot.efi)
 ├─ room.server-mini             (basis + acme, optional cloud-init and qemu-guest)
 │   └─ room.server              (server-mini)
 │       └─ room.server.nas      (server + optional storage services)
 ├─ room.container               (basis + acme, boot.isContainer)
 └─ room.desktop.basis           (basis + desktop hardware and fonts)
     └─ room.desktop.general     (desktop.basis + boot.efi)
         ├─ room.desktop.dev      (desktop.general + dev tools)
         ├─ room.desktop.game     (desktop.general + steam)
         └─ room.desktop.wsl      (desktop.basis + wsl)
```

Home-manager has its own smaller chain and a standalone `room.game`. nix-darwin provides `room.basis` and `room.desktop.dev`.

Because sub-module enables use `lib.mkDefault`, explicit settings take precedence:

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
cattery.apps.jetbrains.enable = false; # use neovim instead
```

***

## What cattery includes

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| **262 modules** | Theming, desktops, gaming, services, CLI tools, development kits, security, and platform integration |
| **Room profiles** | Preset groups such as `room.desktop.dev` and `room.server` |
| **agenix secrets** | Encrypted configuration files for services such as nginx, PostgreSQL, Forgejo, WireGuard, and cloudflared |
| **Impermanence** | Ephemeral root and home with persistent state, including XDG user directories |
| **Platforms** | NixOS, nix-darwin, home-manager, NixOS-WSL, and Proxmox LXC |
| **Overrides** | Most modules accept `extraOptions`, and room defaults use `lib.mkDefault` |

## Module categories

| Category | Modules |
|---|---|
| **Theming** | Catppuccin for GTK, Qt, Plasma, Hyprland, and SDDM |
| **Desktop** | Hyprland (charm-cat and caelestia themes), Niri, GNOME, KDE Plasma configuration |
| **Gaming** | Steam, gale, Heroic, HMCL, AMD GPU |
| **Security** | agenix, impermanence, lanzaboote, YubiKey, GPG |
| **Services** | nginx, PostgreSQL, Forgejo, Gitea, Tailscale, Vaultwarden, Docker, Samba, NFS, ZFS tools, Kubernetes, K3s, monitoring |
| **Dev tools** | VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains, dev-kit (git, nix, rust, go, java, javascript, cpp, lua, wasm, jj, dive), Ollama, Codex |
| **Shell and CLI** | fish, zsh, nushell, direnv, starship, atuin, yazi, neovim, helix |
| **Platform** | NixOS-WSL, Proxmox LXC, nix-darwin, Homebrew |

## Integration modes

The flake exports a module set for each platform:

```nix
# NixOS
imports = [ cattery-modules.nixosModules.default ];

# home-manager
imports = [ cattery-modules.homeModules.default ];

# nix-darwin
imports = [ cattery-modules.darwinModules.default ];
```

# Quick Start

## Installation

Add cattery as a flake input:

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    cattery-modules.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/cattery-modules/*.tar.gz";
  };
}
```

## NixOS

Import the bundled NixOS modules and enable a room:

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    cattery-modules.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/cattery-modules/*.tar.gz";
  };

  outputs = { nixpkgs, cattery-modules, ... }: {
    nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      modules = [
        cattery-modules.nixosModules.default
        ./configuration.nix
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

```nix
# configuration.nix
{ ... }: {
  cattery = {
    room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
    user.name = "alice";
  };
}
```

Then run `nixos-rebuild switch`.

## home-manager

Standalone home-manager works on Linux and macOS and does not need root access:

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    home-manager.url = "github:nix-community/home-manager";
    cattery-modules.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/cattery-modules/*.tar.gz";
  };

  outputs = { nixpkgs, home-manager, cattery-modules, ... }: {
    homeConfigurations.alice = home-manager.lib.homeManagerConfiguration {
      pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
      modules = [
        cattery-modules.homeModules.default
        {
          cattery = {
            room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
            user.name = "alice";
          };
        }
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

```bash
home-manager switch --flake .#alice
```

## nix-darwin

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    darwin.url = "github:nix-darwin/nix-darwin";
    cattery-modules.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/cattery-modules/*.tar.gz";
  };

  outputs = { darwin, cattery-modules, ... }: {
    darwinConfigurations.macbook = darwin.lib.darwinSystem {
      system = "aarch64-darwin";
      modules = [
        cattery-modules.darwinModules.default
        {
          cattery = {
            room.basis.enable = true;
            user.name = "alice";
          };
        }
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

```bash
darwin-rebuild switch --flake .#macbook
```

## NixOS-WSL

```nix
{
  cattery = {
    room.desktop.wsl.enable = true;
    user.name = "alice";
  };
}
```

## Proxmox LXC

```nix
{
  cattery = {
    room.container.enable = true;
    system.proxmox.lxc.manageNetwork = true;
    user.name = "alice";
  };
}
```

## Individual modules

If you do not want a room, enable modules directly:

```nix
{
  cattery = {
    desktop.hyprland.enable = true;
    desktop.addons.catppuccin.enable = true;
    services.tailscale.enable = true;
    cli-apps.dev-kit.git.enable = true;
    cli-apps.dev-kit.rust.enable = true;
    cli-apps.shell.fish.enable = true;
    user.name = "alice";
  };
}
```

## Customizing rooms

Room sub-module enables use `lib.mkDefault`, so you can turn individual modules off or on:

```nix
{
  cattery = {
    room.desktop.dev.enable = true;

    # Override room defaults:
    cli-apps.dev-kit.javascript.enable = false; # use bun standalone
    desktop.hyprland.enable = false;
    desktop.niri.enable = true;
  };
}
```

## User information

Several modules read `cattery.user` for defaults, including git identity, email, GPG, and the login shell:

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }: {
  cattery.user = {
    name = "alice";
    realName = "Alice";
    email = {
      address = "alice@example.com";
      userName = "alice";
    };
    defaultUserShell = pkgs.fish; # also enables the fish module by default
    gpg.signKey = "ABCD1234";
  };
}
```

`cattery.user.home`, `uid`, and `gid` are read-only values taken from the system user.

## Next steps

* [Rooms](/rooms): see what each room enables
* [Modules](/modules): browse the module catalog
* [Secrets and agenix](/secrets): set up encrypted secrets

# Rooms

A room is a module that enables other modules with `lib.mkDefault`. Enabling one room enables its dependencies, so a single option can turn on a set of related features. All sub-module enables use `lib.mkDefault`, so explicit settings take precedence.

The NixOS room graph:

```
room.basis
 ├─ room.general                 (basis + boot.efi)
 ├─ room.server-mini             (basis + acme, optional cloud-init and qemu-guest)
 │   └─ room.server              (server-mini)
 │       └─ room.server.nas      (server + optional storage services)
 ├─ room.container               (basis + acme, boot.isContainer)
 └─ room.desktop.basis           (basis + desktop hardware and fonts)
     └─ room.desktop.general     (desktop.basis + boot.efi)
         ├─ room.desktop.dev      (desktop.general + dev tools)
         ├─ room.desktop.game     (desktop.general + steam)
         └─ room.desktop.wsl      (desktop.basis + wsl)
```

Home-manager has a separate chain and a standalone `room.game`. nix-darwin provides `room.basis` and `room.desktop.dev`.

## How rooms work

Rooms exist in the NixOS, home-manager, and nix-darwin module sets. The NixOS set has the largest graph. The home-manager set has its own chain, and the darwin set has only two rooms. Enabling `desktop.dev` in the NixOS set enables `desktop.general`, then `desktop.basis`, then `basis`.

To override a room, set the individual module option. The room default loses because `lib.mkDefault` has a lower priority than a normal assignment:

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
cattery.apps.jetbrains.enable = false;
```

## NixOS rooms

### room.basis

The base system. It enables `cli-apps.mtr`, `cli-apps.nix.nix-ld`, `services.cron`, `services.openssh`, `system.locale`, `system.network`, `system.time`, and `system.ulimit`. It also enables `nix` and `cli-apps.openssh`, and sets `system.boot.kernel.useLatest` to `true`.

```nix
cattery.room.basis.enable = true;
```

### room.general

`room.basis` plus `system.boot.efi`.

```nix
cattery.room.general.enable = true;
```

### room.server-mini

`room.basis` plus `services.acme`. It also exposes `qemu-guest.enable` and `cloud-init.enable`. Both are off by default.

```nix
cattery.room.server-mini.enable = true;
cattery.room.server-mini.qemu-guest.enable = true;
cattery.room.server-mini.cloud-init.enable = true;
```

### room.server

`room.basis` plus `room.server-mini`. The `qemu-guest` and `cloud-init` options are passed through to `server-mini`.

```nix
cattery.room.server = {
  enable = true;
  qemu-guest.enable = true;
  cloud-init.enable = true;
};
```

### room.server.nas

`room.server` plus a set of storage and monitoring services. `samba`, `avahi`, `samba-wsdd`, `sanoid`, `syncoid`, `beszel`, `nfs`, and `target` are enabled by default. `netdata` and `zfs` are available but off by default. `zfs` requires `networking.hostId`.

```nix
cattery.room.server.nas = {
  enable = true;
  zfs.enable = true;
  netdata.enable = false;
};
```

### room.container

`room.basis` plus `services.acme`. It sets `boot.isContainer = true` and disables `wpa_supplicant`, which cannot start in a container without `/dev/rfkill`.

```nix
cattery.room.container.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.basis

`room.basis` plus `system.automount`, `system.fcitx5`, `system.network.wireless`, `system.peripherals`, `desktop.addons.chromium-support`, `cli-apps.security.fido2`, and `system.fonts`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.basis.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.general

`room.desktop.basis` plus `system.boot.efi`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.general.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.dev

`room.desktop.general` plus `apps.yubikey`, `services.docker`, `services.vscode-server`, and `system.boot.binfmt`. It also sets `security.sudo.wheelNeedsPassword = false`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.game

`room.desktop.general` plus `apps.game.steam`. It also sets `security.sudo.wheelNeedsPassword = false`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.game.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.wsl

`room.desktop.basis` plus `system.wsl`. It also sets `security.sudo.wheelNeedsPassword = false`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.wsl.enable = true;
```

## Home-manager rooms

### room.basis

Enables `cli-apps.dev-kit.git`, `cli-apps.dev-kit.nix`, `cli-apps.tool.gh`, `cli-apps.nix.home-manager`, and `cli-apps.nix.nix-index`.

```nix
cattery.room.basis.enable = true;
```

### room.general

`room.basis` plus shell and CLI tools: `cli-apps.shell.atuin`, `direnv`, `starship`, and `powershell` (Darwin). It also enables `cli-apps.tool.http-utils`, `monitoring`, `network`, `compressor`, `tldr`, and `misc`, sets `cli-apps.tool.useful` with `commonAliases`, and enables `cli-apps.file-manager.yazi`, `cli-apps.disk`, and `cli-apps.misc`.

```nix
cattery.room.general.enable = true;
```

### room.game

Standalone room based on `room.basis`. It enables `apps.vscode`, `apps.zed-editor`, `apps.instant-messengers`, `cli-apps.video.visual`, and `cli-apps.video.youtube`. On Linux it also enables `apps.game`; on Darwin it enables `apps.iina`.

```nix
cattery.room.game.enable = true;
```

### room.server-mini

`room.basis` plus `cli-apps.shell.starship`. It sets `system.impermanence.xdg.userDirs.enable` to `false` by default.

```nix
cattery.room.server-mini.enable = true;
```

### room.server

`room.general` plus `room.server-mini` plus `cli-apps.tool.acme-sh`.

```nix
cattery.room.server.enable = true;
```

### room.container

`room.basis` plus `cli-apps.shell.starship` and `cli-apps.tool.acme-sh`.

```nix
cattery.room.container.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.basis

`room.general` plus `apps.graphics`, `apps.useful`, and `desktop.xdg`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.basis.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.general

`room.desktop.basis` plus `apps.wezterm`, `apps.vscode`, and `apps.zed-editor` (with `defaultEditor` enabled). On Linux it also enables `apps.browser`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.general.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.dev

`room.desktop.general` plus `apps.instant-messengers`, `apps.jetbrains`, `apps.code-cursor`, `cli-apps.database.sqlite`, `cli-apps.operations.cloud`, `cli-apps.operations.kubernetes`, `cli-apps.security.gnupg`, and `cli-apps.tool.ollama`. It also enables `cli-apps.video.visual` and `cli-apps.video.youtube`.

On Linux it enables `apps.thunderbird`, `apps.science`, `apps.video`, `cli-apps.cloudflared`, and `cli-apps.warp`. On Darwin it enables `apps.iina` and `cli-apps.android`.

The `allDevKit` option enables `cli-apps.dev-kit.cpp`, `dive`, `go`, `java` (with Maven and Gradle), `javascript`, `lua`, `rust`, and `wasm`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev = {
  enable = true;
  allDevKit = true;
};
```

### room.desktop.game

`room.desktop.general` plus `apps.instant-messengers`. On Linux it also enables `apps.game`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.game.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.wsl

`room.desktop.basis` only.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.wsl.enable = true;
```

### room.server.nas

`room.server` plus `cli-apps.tool.useful` and `cli-apps.disk`.

```nix
cattery.room.server.nas.enable = true;
```

## nix-darwin rooms

### room.basis

Enables `brew`, `system.sudoTouch`, `system.useful`, `nix`, `cli-apps.openssh`, `system.fonts`, and `system.ulimit` with `openFilesLimit = 4096`.

```nix
cattery.room.basis.enable = true;
```

### room.desktop.dev

`room.basis` plus `cli-apps.security.fido2`.

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
```

## Customizing rooms

All rooms use `lib.mkDefault` for sub-module enables, so explicit configuration wins:

```nix
cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;

cattery.desktop.hyprland.enable = false;
cattery.desktop.niri.enable = true;          # use niri
cattery.apps.jetbrains.enable = false;        # use neovim
cattery.cli-apps.shell.fish.enable = false;
cattery.cli-apps.shell.zsh.enable = true;
```

The login shell modules also read `cattery.user.defaultUserShell`. Setting that to `pkgs.fish`, `pkgs.zsh`, or `pkgs.nushell` enables the matching module by default.

## Composing multiple rooms

Rooms can be enabled together. Shared dependencies are enabled once, and each room adds its own modules:

```nix
cattery = {
  room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
  room.desktop.game.enable = true;
};
```

## Rooms compared with individual modules

| Approach | Use when |
|---|---|
| Room | You want a working set of related modules with defaults to override |
| Individual modules | You want to choose every module yourself |

You can start with a room and then disable or add individual modules.

# Modules

cattery defines 262 module files under the `cattery` namespace. The count includes room profiles and `secrets` companion modules. Enable modules individually or use a room. The tables below list the modules and their main options. See the module source for the full option set.

## Theming

### cattery.desktop.addons.catppuccin

Catppuccin theming for the desktop environment. The module exists in the NixOS and home-manager sets.

```nix
cattery.desktop.addons.catppuccin.enable = true;
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `enable` | Enable Catppuccin |
| `autoEnable` | Enable all Catppuccin integrations by default. Defaults to the value of `enable` |
| `extraOptions` | Extra options merged into the Catppuccin configuration |

## Desktop

### Compositors and display managers

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland` | Hyprland with XWayland (NixOS). The home-manager module adds `require` and `on` event callbacks | `enable`, `require`, `on` |
| `cattery.desktop.niri` | Niri configuration (home-manager) | `enable`, `configText`, `include`, `spawnAtStartup`, `binds` |
| `cattery.desktop.plasma` | KDE Plasma configuration through plasma-manager (home-manager) | `enable`, `settings` |
| `cattery.desktop.gnome` | GNOME with GDM (NixOS) | `enable` |
| `cattery.desktop.lightdm` | LightDM (NixOS) | `enable` |

### Hyprland themes

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat` | Hyprland theme with waybar, kitty, anyrun, hyprlock, mako, wlogout, and awww wallpaper | `enable`, `greetd.enable` (NixOS) |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia` | Caelestia theme with SDDM on NixOS. The home-manager module provides settings and persistence | `enable`, `settings`, `persistence` |

### Charm-cat sub-modules

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.audio` | pipewire, wireplumber, pavucontrol, brightnessctl |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.convention` | Workspace conventions, keybinds, monitor rules |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.fcitx` | Fcitx5 input method integration |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.file-manager` | Dolphin file manager |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.launcher` | Anyrun with plugins |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.lock-screen` | Hyprlock and hypridle screen lock |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.notification` | Mako notification daemon |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.screenshots` | Hyprshot, grim, slurp, and wl-clipboard |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.terminal` | Kitty with JetBrains Mono Nerd Font |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.vscode` | VS Code workspace integration |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.wallpaper` | Awww wallpaper rotation |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.waybar` | Waybar configuration |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.charm-cat.wlogout` | Wlogout power menu |

### Caelestia sub-modules

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.convention` | Settings, workspace action script, workspace switching |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.audio` | pipewire, wireplumber, pavucontrol, brightnessctl |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.fcitx` | Fcitx5 integration |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.file-manager` | Thunar with archive and volume plugins |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.idle` | Hypridle and the caelestia shell lock |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.screenshots` | Hyprshot screenshot tool |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.theme.caelestia.terminal` | Kitty with JetBrains Mono Nerd Font |

### Desktop addons

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.addons.xdg-portal` | XDG Desktop Portal with wlr | `enable` |
| `cattery.desktop.addons.chromium-support` | Wayland Chromium and Electron (`NIXOS_OZONE_WL=1`) | `enable` |
| `cattery.desktop.xdg` | MIME default applications (home-manager) | `app.browser`, `app.editor`, `app.audio`, `app.image`, `app.video`, `app.mailto`, `app.calendar` |

### Hyprland addons

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.addons.hyprshot` | Screenshot tool (hyprshot, grim, slurp) |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.addons.hyprlock` | Screen locker |
| `cattery.desktop.hyprland.addons.hypridle` | Idle management daemon |

## Gaming

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.apps.game.steam` | Steam with protonup-qt, remote play, and hardware support | `enable`, `persistence` |
| `cattery.apps.game.gale` | Gale game launcher | `enable`, `persistence` |
| `cattery.apps.game` | Heroic Games Launcher and r2modman (home-manager) | `enable` |
| `cattery.apps.hmcl` | HMCL Minecraft launcher | `enable`, `persistence` |
| `cattery.system.gpu.amd` | AMD GPU driver (`amdgpu` kernel module) | `enable` |

## Security

### Secrets (agenix)

See the [Secrets and agenix](/secrets) page for setup details.

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.secrets` | agenix secrets with host, shared, and user scopes | `enable`, `yubikey.enable`, `secretsDir`, `secretsMountPoint`, `secretsPath`, `hosts`, `shared`, `files` |
| `cattery.nix.secrets` | Encrypted Nix configuration included through `nix.extraOptions` | `enable`, `scope`, `etc.enable`, `etc.useSymlink`, `etc.dirPath`, `files` |

### Impermanence

See [Impermanence](/impermanence) for setup examples and the full list of persisted paths.

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.system.impermanence` | Ephemeral root with persistent state (NixOS) | `enable`, `directories`, `files`, `persistencePath`, `extraOptions` |
| `cattery.system.impermanence` | Ephemeral home with persistent state (home-manager) | `enable`, `directories`, `files`, `persistencePath`, `xdg.userDirs`, `xdg.cache`, `xdg.config`, `xdg.data`, `xdg.state`, `extraOptions` |
| `cattery.system.fileSystems.btrfs.impermanence` | BTRFS subvolume rolling for impermanence | Per subvolume: `device`, `tempDir`, `oldSubvolDir`, `subvol` |

The home-manager module persists `.ssh`, `.pki`, and the XDG user directories by default.

`xdg.userDirs` has `enable` and a read-only `full`. `xdg.cache`, `xdg.config`, `xdg.data`, and `xdg.state` add `directories` and `files`. Set `xdg.userDirs.projects = null` to skip the `Projects` directory introduced by `xdg-user-dirs` 0.20.

### Secure Boot

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.system.boot.lanzaboote` | Secure Boot with lanzaboote | `enable`, `pkiBundle`, `extraOptions` |

### Other security

|---|---|---|
| `cattery.security.pam` | PAM configuration passthrough | Attribute set merged into `security.pam` |

| `cattery.apps.safety` | Bitwarden desktop (home-manager) | `enable` |

## User

### cattery.user

Core user configuration. Many modules read these values for defaults.

| Option | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | User name |
| `realName` | null or str | Full name, used for the Git user name |
| `email.address` | null or str | Email address |
| `email.userName` | null or str | Mail account user name, defaults to `email.address` |
| `email.imap` | null or submodule | IMAP settings with `host` and `port` |
| `email.smtp` | null or submodule | SMTP settings with `host` and `port` |
| `defaultUserShell` | null or path or package | Login shell, for example `pkgs.fish`. The matching shell module enables by default |
| `gpg.signKey` | null or str | GPG signing key |
| `gpg.encryptKey` | null or str | GPG encryption key |
| `initialHashedPassword` | null or str | Initial user password hash |
| `useSecretPasswordFile` | bool | Read the password from an agenix secret |
| `authorizedKeys.keys` | list of str | SSH authorized keys |
| `authorizedKeys.keyFiles` | list of path | Files containing SSH authorized keys |
| `settings` | attrs | Extra values consumed by theme and desktop modules |
| `home` | null or str | Home directory (read-only) |
| `uid` | null or int | User ID (read-only) |
| `gid` | null or int | Group ID (read-only) |

### cattery.home

home-manager bridge. It forwards `extraOptions` to `home-manager.users.<name>`.

| Option | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `extraOptions` | attrs | Extra home-manager options |

## Darwin-specific

| Module | Description | Options |
|---|---|---|
| `cattery.services.openssh` | OpenSSH on macOS | `enable`, `extraConfig`, `extraOptions` |
| `cattery.cli-apps.android` | android-tools (Darwin) | `enable` |
| `cattery.home` | home-manager bridge on Darwin | `extraOptions` |

***

Most modules accept an `extraOptions` attribute set that is merged into the underlying NixOS or home-manager options. Many home-manager modules that write state also expose a `persistence` option, default `true`, which registers paths with `cattery.system.impermanence`.

# Secrets & agenix

cattery integrates [agenix](https://github.com/ryantm/agenix) for encrypted secrets. Service modules that need configuration files have a companion `secrets` module. The companion module adds the encrypted files to `age.secrets`. Many of these modules also link the decrypted file into `/etc`.

## File layout

`cattery.secrets.secretsPath` defaults to `<user.home>/agenix`. The files under that directory are grouped by scope:

```
<secretsPath>/
├── hosts/<host>/global/        # host-specific, root-owned
├── hosts/<host>/users/<user>/  # host-specific, user-owned
├── shared/global/              # shared across hosts, root-owned
└── shared/users/<user>/        # shared across hosts, user-owned
```

If you keep secrets in your flake, point the option at that directory:

```nix
cattery.secrets.secretsPath = ./secrets;
```

The keys in `secrets.nix` must match the file paths under `secretsPath`.

## Enabling secrets

```nix
{
  cattery.secrets.enable = true;
}
```

`enable` installs the agenix CLI and generates `age.secrets` from the configured files. `cattery.secrets.secretsDir` and `cattery.secrets.secretsMountPoint` are passed to agenix when set.

## Service secrets

Most companion modules enable themselves when both the parent service and `cattery.secrets` are enabled:

```nix
cattery = {
  secrets.enable = true;

  services.nginx.enable = true;      # encrypted nginx conf.d files
  services.forgejo.enable = true;    # encrypted Forgejo app.ini when useWizard is set
  services.postgresql.enable = true; # encrypted PostgreSQL config when useWizard is set
  services.wg-quick = {
    enable = true;
    configNames = [ "wg0" ];
  };
  services.cloudflared.enable = true; # encrypted tunnel credentials
};
```

For services with a host configuration file, set `useWizard = true` on the service to use the encrypted file instead of declarative settings.

`cattery.nix.secrets` is different: it is disabled by default. Set `cattery.nix.secrets.enable = true` to add the encrypted include to `nix.extraOptions`.

## Secret modules

| Module | Secret files |
|---|---|
| `cattery.secrets` | Main secrets configuration (hosts, shared, files) |
| `cattery.nix.secrets` | Encrypted Nix configuration included through `nix.extraOptions` |
| `cattery.services.nginx.secrets` | nginx `conf.d` files |
| `cattery.services.acme.secrets` | ACME DNS provider environment files |
| `cattery.services.adguardhome.secrets` | `AdGuardHome.yaml` when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.forgejo.secrets` | Forgejo `app.ini` when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.gitea.secrets` | Gitea `app.ini` when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.gitea-actions-runner.secrets` | Runner token environment files |
| `cattery.services.postgresql.secrets` | PostgreSQL configuration when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.vaultwarden.secrets` | Vaultwarden environment file |
| `cattery.services.cloudflared.secrets` | Tunnel credential files |
| `cattery.services.wg-quick.secrets` | WireGuard configuration files |
| `cattery.services.sing-box.secrets` | sing-box `config.json` |
| `cattery.services.samba.secrets` | Samba `smb.conf` when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.nfs.secrets` | NFS exports file when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.sanoid.secrets` | Sanoid configuration when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.target.secrets` | iSCSI target configuration when `useWizard` is set |
| `cattery.services.beszel.secrets` | Beszel agent environment file |
| `cattery.system.fileSystems.samba.secrets` | Samba client credential files |
| `cattery.system.fileSystems.webdav.secrets` | WebDAV credentials |
| `cattery.cli-apps.ssh.secrets` | SSH include files (home-manager) or known hosts files (NixOS) |
| `cattery.cli-apps.security.gnupg.secrets` | GnuPG files |
| `cattery.cli-apps.dev-kit.git.secrets` | Git include configuration |

## Secret scopes

| Scope | Path | Owner | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hosts-global` | `hosts/<host>/global/` | root | System configuration for one host |
| `hosts-user` | `hosts/<host>/users/<user>/` | user | User configuration for one host |
| `shared-global` | `shared/global/` | root | System configuration shared by all hosts |
| `shared-user` | `shared/users/<user>/` | user | User configuration shared by all hosts |

Not every module uses the same default scope. For example, `cattery.services.acme.secrets`, `cattery.services.cloudflared.secrets`, and `cattery.system.fileSystems.samba.secrets` default to `shared-global`. The module source sets the default for each companion module.

## Setting up secrets

1. Generate an age identity if you do not already have one:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/age
age-keygen -o ~/.config/age/keys.txt
```

If `age-keygen` is not installed, use `nix run nixpkgs#age -- keygen -o ~/.config/age/keys.txt`.

2. Add the public key to `secrets.nix`. The file lists each encrypted file and its recipients:

```nix
# secrets.nix
{
  "hosts/server/global/nginx.conf.age".publicKeys = [ alice server ];
}
```

3. Encrypt the file. Run the command from the directory that contains `secrets.nix`:

```bash
cd ~/agenix
nix run github:ryantm/agenix -- -e hosts/server/global/nginx.conf.age
```

If you set `cattery.secrets.secretsPath = ./secrets`, run the same command from that directory.

4. Add the identity to the host. On NixOS, agenix reads the host SSH keys by default. To use the key generated in step 1:

```nix
{
  age.identityPaths = [ "/home/alice/.config/age/keys.txt" ];
}
```

5. Enable the service and the secrets module:

```nix
cattery = {
  secrets.enable = true;
  services.nginx.enable = true;
};
```

The file is decrypted during activation and linked to its target, for example `/etc/nginx/conf.d/nginx.conf`.

## YubiKey support

`cattery.secrets.yubikey.enable` is declared, but the current module does not add `age-plugin-yubikey`. The package override is commented out in `modules/shared/secrets/default.nix`, so enabling the option alone does not configure a YubiKey identity. To use a YubiKey, add the plugin and the identity path through the agenix options.

## Impermanence and secrets

When `cattery.system.impermanence.enable` is set on NixOS, the module persists `/etc/ssh` and sets `age.identityPaths` to the copies under `/persistent/etc/ssh`. The host keys used by agenix then survive reboots. The home-manager impermanence module does the same for the user's `.ssh` directory. Decrypted secrets stay in the agenix runtime directory (normally `/run/agenix`); the impermanence modules do not copy them to the persistent volume. See [Impermanence](/impermanence) for the full path list.

```nix
cattery = {
  secrets.enable = true;
  system.impermanence.enable = true;
};
```

# Impermanence

cattery has two impermanence modules. The NixOS module persists system paths; the home-manager module persists user state. Both wrap [nix-community/impermanence](https://github.com/nix-community/impermanence) and default to `/persistent`.

## NixOS

```nix
{
  cattery.system.impermanence = {
    enable = true;
    directories = [
      "/var/lib/my-service"
    ];
    files = [
      "/etc/my-service.conf"
    ];
  };
}
```

`environment.persistence."/persistent"` gets these entries by default:

| Path | Type |
|---|---|
| `/var/log` | directory |
| `/var/lib` | directory |
| `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections` | directory |
| `/etc/ssh` | directory |
| `/etc/machine-id` | file |

`directories` and `files` append to that list. `extraOptions` is merged into the same attribute set.

The module also points `age.identityPaths` at the SSH host keys under `/persistent`, so agenix can decrypt host secrets after a reboot.

## home-manager

```nix
{
  cattery.system.impermanence = {
    enable = true;
    xdg.userDirs.projects = null;
  };
}
```

The module only writes persistence entries when `home.persistence` exists. In a NixOS + home-manager setup, that happens when `impermanence.nixosModules.impermanence` and `home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager` are imported; `cattery.nixosModules.default` includes both. Don't import `impermanence.homeManagerModules.*` yourself. Standalone home-manager has no `home.persistence`, so the module does nothing.

`directories` and `files` add paths on top of the defaults. `extraOptions` is merged into `home.persistence."/persistent"`.

Default entries:

| Path | Notes |
|---|---|
| `.ssh` | directory, mode `0700` |
| `.pki` | directory, mode `0700` |
| XDG user directories | Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Music, Pictures, Projects, Public, Templates, Videos |
| `~/.cache` | only the listed entries unless `xdg.cache.full` is true |
| `~/.config` | only the listed entries unless `xdg.config.full` is true |
| `~/.local/share` | only the listed entries unless `xdg.data.full` is true |
| `~/.local/state` | only the listed entries unless `xdg.state.full` is true |

The module also points `age.identityPaths` at `.ssh/id_ed25519` and `.ssh/id_rsa` under `/persistent`.

### XDG user directories

`xdg.userDirs.enable` is `true` by default, and `xdg.userDirs.full` cannot be turned off. Every non-null XDG directory is persisted:

```text
Desktop
Documents
Downloads
Music
Pictures
Projects
Public
Templates
Videos
```

`Projects` comes from `xdg-user-dirs` 0.20 and Home Manager's `xdg.userDirs.projects`. To skip it:

```nix
{
  cattery.system.impermanence.xdg.userDirs.projects = null;
}
```

Null entries are filtered out before they reach impermanence. Setting the option to `null` also clears `XDG_PROJECTS_DIR`, so Home Manager stops creating `~/Projects`.

### XDG cache, config, data, and state

Each of `xdg.cache`, `xdg.config`, `xdg.data`, and `xdg.state` has:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enable` | `true` | Include this XDG base directory |
| `full` | `false` | Persist the whole base directory |
| `directories` | `[ ]` | Subdirectories to persist |
| `files` | `[ ]` | Files to persist |

Without `full`, only the entries in `directories` and `files` are persisted.

```nix
{
  cattery.system.impermanence = {
    xdg = {
      config.directories = [ "my-app" ];
      data.files = [ "my-app/state.db" ];
      cache.directories = [ "my-app/cache" ];
    };
  };
}
```

## BTRFS rollback

`cattery.system.fileSystems.btrfs.impermanence` runs in initrd. It snapshots the current subvolume, deletes it, creates a fresh one, then mounts root. Configure one entry per subvolume:

```nix
{
  cattery.system.fileSystems.btrfs.impermanence."@home".device =
    "/dev/disk/by-uuid/2f1dc58e-6d8a-4cb4-8247-b4e9acf39681";
}
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `device` | required | Block device containing the subvolume |
| `subvol` | entry name | Subvolume to roll back |
| `tempDir` | `/btrfs_<subvol>_tmp` | Temporary mount point |
| `oldSubvolDir` | `old_<subvol>` | Where old snapshots are kept |

Archives older than 30 days are deleted.

## Secrets

The NixOS module persists `/etc/ssh`; the home-manager module persists `.ssh`. Decrypted secrets stay in `/run/agenix` and are not copied to `/persistent`.

# Contributing

cattery-modules follows [GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow) with `main` as the trunk branch.

## Development environment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nixcafe/cattery-modules.git
cd cattery-modules
nix develop
```

The dev shell provides:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `nixfmt` | Nix code formatter |
| `deadnix` | Find dead or unused Nix code |
| `statix` | Lint Nix files (`repeated_keys` disabled) |

The shell hook installs the pre-commit hooks. If you use direnv, `direnv allow` loads the same shell.

## Project structure

```
cattery-modules/
├── flake.nix                  # Flake entrypoint using purr.lib.mkFlake
├── modules/
│   ├── nixos/                 # NixOS modules
│   │   ├── room/              # Room profiles
│   │   ├── services/          # Services (nginx, postgresql, ...)
│   │   ├── desktop/           # Compositors, themes, display managers
│   │   ├── apps/              # NixOS-side application modules
│   │   ├── cli-apps/          # NixOS-side CLI modules
│   │   ├── system/            # Boot, GPU, network, locale, file systems
│   │   ├── security/          # PAM
│   │   └── containers/        # Declarative NixOS containers
│   ├── home/                  # home-manager modules
│   │   ├── room/              # Home-manager room profiles
│   │   ├── shared/            # Cross-platform home modules
│   │   ├── nixos/             # NixOS-specific home modules
│   │   └── darwin/            # Darwin-specific home modules
│   ├── darwin/                # nix-darwin modules
│   └── shared/                # Modules shared between module sets
├── lib/
│   ├── module/                # mkDefaultEnabled, mkDefaultDisabled
│   ├── secrets/               # agenix helper functions
│   └── utils/                 # General utilities
├── shells/                    # Dev shell definition
└── checks/                    # git-hooks and module-eval checks
```

## Module conventions

Most modules follow this shape:

```nix
{
  config,
  lib,
  namespace,
  pkgs,
  ...
}:
let
  cfg = config.${namespace}.my-module;
in
{
  options.${namespace}.my-module = {
    enable = lib.mkEnableOption "my module";
    # ... other options
  };

  config = lib.mkIf cfg.enable {
    # ... implementation
  };
}
```

### Key conventions

* **Namespace**: Use `${namespace}`. The flake sets it to `cattery`.
* **Enable option**: Most modules have an `enable` option.
* **extraOptions**: Many modules expose `extraOptions = mkOption { type = attrs; default = { }; }` and merge it into the underlying options.
* **persistence**: Many home-manager modules that write state have a `persistence` option, default `true`.
* **Platform checks**: Use `purr.meta.isLinux` and `purr.meta.isDarwin` for platform-specific code.
* **Rooms**: Use `mkDefaultEnabled` from `lib.cattery.module` for sub-module enables.

## Branch naming

| Prefix | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `feat/` | New features or modules |
| `fix/` | Bug fixes |
| `chore/` | Maintenance and dependency updates |
| `docs/` | Documentation |

## Workflow

1. Create a branch from `main`.

2. Make changes.

3. Test locally:

   ```bash
   nix flake check     # lint and evaluate all 262 modules
   nix fmt             # format all files
   ```

4. Optionally test on a real machine:

   ```bash
   nixos-rebuild test --flake .#myhost
   home-manager switch --flake .#alice
   ```

5. Push the branch and open a pull request against `main`.

6. Get at least one review approval.

7. On merge to `main`, FlakeHub publishes a new rolling release.

## CI

Pull requests to `main` run `nix flake check`. The check includes:

* **nixfmt**: format check
* **deadnix**: dead code check
* **statix**: lint check
* **module-eval**: import and call check for all 262 module files

A push to `main` triggers the FlakeHub workflow, which publishes a rolling release at `nixcafe/cattery-modules`.

## Adding a module

1. Create the module file in the appropriate directory:
   * NixOS: `modules/nixos/<category>/<name>/default.nix`
   * Shared between module sets: `modules/shared/<category>/<name>/default.nix`
   * Cross-platform home-manager: `modules/home/shared/<category>/<name>/default.nix`
   * NixOS-specific home-manager: `modules/home/nixos/<category>/<name>/default.nix`
   * Darwin-specific home-manager: `modules/home/darwin/<category>/<name>/default.nix`

2. Add `enable` and any module-specific options. Add `extraOptions` when the module wraps a NixOS or home-manager option set.

3. If the module needs secrets, add a companion `secrets/default.nix` and use `mkAppSecretsOption` or `mkHomeAppSecretsOption` from `lib.cattery.secrets`.

4. Add the module to a room when appropriate. Use `mkDefaultEnabled` for sub-module enables.

5. Run `nix flake check` and `nix fmt`.

## Branch protection

* Pull request reviews are required (at least one approval).
* Status checks must pass before merging.
* Stale reviews are dismissed when new commits are pushed.
